description:
You are a digital forensics analyst at a human rights organization. A field operative's Tor Browser session has been compromised and you must perform an emergency lockdown procedure before the browser is handed to a forensics team. The lockdown procedure requires ALL of the following steps in Tor Browser:

1. SECURITY HARDENING: Change the Security Level to 'Safest' (shield icon in toolbar)

2. EVIDENCE CAPTURE: Take a screenshot of the current state by pressing PrintScreen or using the system screenshot tool. Save it as /home/ga/Desktop/incident_screenshot.png (use the GNOME screenshot tool by pressing PrintScreen, or from the Applications menu, or via the terminal with: 'DISPLAY=:1 scrot /home/ga/Desktop/incident_screenshot.png')

3. HISTORY EXPORT: Visit 'https://check.torproject.org/' to document the current exit node, then use the Tor Browser address bar to navigate to 'about:config' and set 'privacy.clearOnShutdown.history' to true

4. DATA CLEARING: Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Clear Data (or History > Clear Recent History). Clear ALL of the following: Browsing History, Download History, Active Logins, Cookies and Cache, Offline Website Data. Select 'Everything' for the time range.

5. CONFIGURATION LOCK: In about:config, set 'browser.privatebrowsing.autostart' to true (forces private browsing mode for all future sessions)

6. SAVE INCIDENT REPORT: Write a brief incident report to /home/ga/Desktop/incident_report.txt containing at minimum the text 'LOCKDOWN COMPLETE' and the current date

All 6 steps must be completed. The incident_screenshot.png and incident_report.txt files must exist on the Desktop when complete.
